intent: Every gaming keyboard I look at advertises 8000Hz polling, optical switches with supposedly zero debounce delay, and full N-key rollover like they're life-changing. My friend insists that past a basic level none of it is humanly perceptible, yet buyer reviews are full of people swearing their aim got better the day the box arrived. Before I pay a premium for the spec-sheet flagship, I want to know which of these features are physically real advantages, which are placebo, and whether there's a sensibly priced board that already has the ones that genuinely matter.
author_notes: Deep-tier task v1 — see configs/deep_topics/V1_TASK_DESIGN_GRID.md §2 for spec.
intent_v1_legacy: I'm slowly turning my house into a smart home, locks, cameras, a hub, plugs, but the protocol soup is doing my head in: Wi-Fi, Z-Wave, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Bluetooth LE, and more. My real worry is security, this stuff controls my front door. Can you map out every wireless protocol these devices actually use and how each one handles pairing, encryption, and known weaknesses, plus how reliable people find them day to day? I care a lot about cloud versus local-only control. And please warn me about anything I should flat-out avoid.

tri_source.angle: Gaming spec-sheet claims (8000Hz polling, optical 'zero debounce', full N-key rollover): which are humanly perceptible vs marketing
